disposition_mapping.rationale: Council consensus (pragmatist, finance_domain, emerging_economy, hitl_designer, agentic_architect, accounting_standards) rejected automating away the confirmation act itself. Status aggregation may be automated, but the GL accountant's affirmative confirmation on exception survives as a named, time-stamped human act, preserving KB-03 reporting-period discipline and FSP-R-10.

Agentic_architect's round-2 concession to hitl_designer is adopted: the mechanical/judgment split must be a step-boundary distinction, not a queue buried inside one step's prose, or the estimate-approval function risks becoming a ceremonial checkpoint (KB-04, KB-10). Mechanical, rules-based postings are automated in TS-02a; estimation entries are held in an explicit blocking queue with a named human approver in TS-02b. Both target steps consume the approved adjustment schedule (FSP-R-02); TS-02b additionally consumes revenue cut-off evidence (FSP-R-06), since cut-off judgment calls are the estimation-adjacent subset of this function.

Finance_domain's mechanical correction, accepted across the council (pragmatist conceded, emerging_economy, agentic_architect, accounting_standards, hitl_designer converged), establishes that intercompany elimination cannot be correctly performed until both sides of a balance are in a common currency - the baseline's parallel branch design obscured this dependency. Consolidation and translation are merged into one Group-accountant step with elimination completeness (KB-14) preserved as an explicit, separately logged output and a blocking exception path for unmatched items, satisfying FSP-R-03.

Same merge as FSP-03, for the same reason: translation is logically integral to correct elimination, not a parallel track. Closing and average exchange rates remain an explicit consumed input (FSP-R-04), and translation differences remain a separately tracked, non-netted output routed to OCI (KB-07, KB-08), as insisted on by finance_domain, hitl_designer, agentic_architect, accounting_standards and emerging_economy.

Mapping is retained as its own step rather than folded into drafting (pragmatist reversed to this position in round 2; finance_domain, emerging_economy and agentic_architect held it throughout) because it crosses the Group-accountant-to-Financial-reporting accountability boundary and because chart-of-accounts hygiene cannot be assumed clean enough for unsupervised auto-mapping across all entities (emerging_economy). The crosswalk is automated with a mandatory, explicit exception queue for new/reclassified accounts. The statement line-item structure remains an explicit input (FSP-R-05).

Drafting survives as its own step (FSP-R-11), performed by Financial reporting and explicitly consuming the accounting policy change and prior-period error record (FSP-R-07, KB-05, KB-06). Agent-assisted first-pass drafting is permitted but Financial reporting remains accountable author of record, preserving actor separation from approval (FSP-R-08) against TS-07.

Although unconstrained_by_design, a strong majority (pragmatist, finance_domain, emerging_economy, hitl_designer, accounting_standards) rejected maximalist's proposal to absorb tie-out into drafting as a silent precondition, on the grounds that a drafter checking their own tie-out is not an independent control and that KB-02's evidential trail requires a discrete, dated artifact. The function is restructured to run as a continuous automated check with a reviewer distinct from the drafter who exercises materiality judgment and formally closes out the result - combining agentic_architect's/hitl_designer's observability gains with the council's insistence on a genuine, non-ceremonial human checkpoint.

Universally preserved as the non-delegable, human-anchored management sign-off (FSP-R-09), distinct in actor from drafting (FSP-R-08). Per hitl_designer's non-negotiable, the review package is widened to surface exceptions, estimates and disclosure items substantively, not just a polished draft.

Despite being unconstrained_by_design, a strong majority (pragmatist, finance_domain, emerging_economy, hitl_designer, and agentic_architect's gated design) rejected merging release into approval: release carries distinct actors, timing, statutory tagging/filing mechanics, and - most importantly - a recall window between internal approval and external submission that a single combined action would eliminate. Release is retained as its own step, triggered against a verified approval flag, with an explicit logged human authorization act and a short retraction window.

steps.description: Subledger close status and reconciliation completeness are aggregated automatically into a close-readiness dashboard. Where all items are clear, the dashboard stages the closed, reconciled trial balance; where any item is open, stale, or flagged, the GL accountant investigates the exception and makes the affirmative confirmation decision. Automation compiles status; it does not replace the confirming act.
steps.name: Automated close-readiness confirmation

steps.description: Recurring, rules-based period-end adjustments (standard accrual reversals, scheduled deferral releases, deterministic cut-off entries) are proposed and posted against the approved adjustment schedule by an automated posting engine. Every posting is logged and reversible by journal reversal, not file edit.
steps.name: Automated mechanical adjustment posting

steps.description: Estimation-based entries (provisions, impairments, NRV write-downs, judgmental revenue cut-off calls) drawn from the approved adjustment schedule and revenue cut-off evidence are staged into an explicit, blocking queue. The GL accountant (or controller) reviews and approves each item with a documented basis before posting; nothing in this category is auto-posted on confidence score alone.
steps.name: Estimate-based adjustment review and approval

steps.description: Entity trial balances are consolidated; foreign subsidiary balances are translated at closing and average rates as an integral first pass so that intercompany balances are expressed in a common currency before matching; intercompany balances and transactions are then matched and eliminated in full. Unmatched intercompany items and rate-feed anomalies are not auto-resolved - they escalate as blocking exceptions to the Group accountant. Translation differences (to OCI) and intercompany elimination completeness remain two separately logged, non-netted outputs of this single pass.
steps.name: Consolidate, eliminate intercompany balances, and translate foreign operations

steps.description: The consolidated and translated trial balance is mapped to the statement line-item structure via a maintained, version-controlled crosswalk. New or unmapped accounts and structural changes are routed to Financial reporting as an exception requiring an explicit mapping decision before the line proceeds; this boundary is kept distinct because it is where the Group accountant's output becomes Financial reporting's input.
steps.name: Automated mapping to statement line items with exception review

steps.description: The primary statements and key notes (accounting policies, revenue, FX, errors, and other required disclosures) are drafted. Tooling may generate a first-pass draft from mapped data, but Financial reporting remains the accountable author of record, explicitly reviewing the accounting policy change and prior-period error record rather than letting it be summarized away.
inputs: Accounting policy change and prior-period error record
steps.name: Draft primary statements and key notes

steps.description: An automated tie-out check runs continuously as the draft evolves, tracing drafted figures back to the trial balance and supporting schedules and maintaining a running variance log. A reviewer distinct from the drafter exercises materiality judgment over unresolved variances and formally closes out tie-out, producing dated tie-out evidence before the draft proceeds to management review. Unresolved variances block progression; they are never silently auto-closed.
steps.name: Analytical review and tie-out

steps.description: Management reviews and approves the financial statements. The review package explicitly surfaces estimate-based adjustments and their basis, consolidation/elimination and translation exceptions, mapping exceptions, and the policy-change/error disclosure record, not merely a clean final draft, so that approval is substantive rather than a formality.
steps.name: Management review and approval

steps.description: Once management approval is recorded, packaging and transmission of the statements (filing systems, portals, distribution) is triggered strictly against a verified approved-statements flag. A CFO or CFO-delegate performs an explicit, logged authorization act distinct from the approval decision itself, with a short retraction window before external transmission is finalized.
steps.name: Release / submission
